title: Word Break
prompt:
Given a string `s` and a dictionary `wordDict`, return whether `s` can be segmented into a sequence of dictionary words (words reusable).

**Example**: `s = "leetcode"`, dict `["leet","code"]` → `true`.

dp[i] = 'the first i characters can be segmented' — true if some split point j has dp[j] true and s[j..i] is a word.
hints: Put the dictionary in a HashSet. dp[0] = true (empty string).
For each end i, look for a split j where dp[j] is true and s.substring(j, i) is a word.

solution.explanation: dp[i] asks 'is the prefix of length i segmentable?' — true when a reachable earlier boundary j is followed by a dictionary word ending at i. Building left to right, dp[n] answers the whole string. O(n²) substrings × set lookup.
